dedupe_keys.name: nweld us national water and energy land dataset

description: NWELD maps the land used by each stage of the US energy sector life cycle, and related water sources for energy, as consistent 30 m raster layers so that energy, water and land can be analysed together. It covers the conterminous United States in 86 layers for coal, hydropower, natural gas, petroleum, solar, wind, biomass, general renewables, infrastructure and water, spanning extraction, development, production, storage, distribution and operation, with infrastructure layers such as transmission lines, railroad tracks, roads, flood control dams and irrigation dams; each layer marks presence with a value of 1. It was produced by J. Sturtevant, R. A. McManamay and C. R. DeRolph and described in Scientific Data in April 2022, with OpenStreetMap features retrieved through R and processing in ArcMap. The data are available for download from figshare as zipped rasters (about 5 GB, 1.32 GB compressed) under CC BY 4.0, free of charge. Caveats: layers record presence only, not capacity or flow, and sources have different dates. It supports mapping of energy and water infrastructure footprints for exposure, land-use conflict and interdependency analysis across sectors; a related record is HIFLD Open.
